title: 3-Read Friday #126: Mini-Whiteboards, PowerPoint, and Math Animations
author: Craig Barton
summary: This is Craig Barton's weekly Eedi curated digest, 3-Read Friday #126, in which he picks three blog posts and adds a short editorial note on each. The first is Anna Sutton's sequel to her mini-whiteboard post, which he describes as arguing that whiteboards are instructional decision-making tools and that none of it works without proper training. The second is Tom Lynch's case for PowerPoint, which holds that teachers make better decisions before a lesson than during it and shows real slides to rebut the claim that a pre-planned deck cannot be responsive. The third is Colin Foster's Two-Minute Math, where pairing an animation tool with AI coding help made it easy to produce more than 160 short explanatory videos. Barton's framing highlights what he found useful in each piece and teases the surprising twist in how Foster would use his videos. The three linked posts are archived separately as their own entries, and the email closes with promotion of Barton's books and community, which is excluded.
points: Barton selects Sutton's mini-whiteboard post as a sequel, with the key claim that whiteboards are the most reliable way to see what every pupil is thinking before deciding the next step.
Lynch's pro-PowerPoint piece is framed around the idea that planning decisions made before the lesson beat improvisation during it, backed by his actual slides.
Foster's project shows how AI coding assistance lowers the cost of producing short, minimalist explanation videos at scale.
Taken together, the three picks all concern how teachers prepare and present explanations, with whiteboards for checking, slides for sequencing and animations for modelling.
